videos.title: Essentials: Neuralink & Technologies to Enhance Human Brains | Dr. Matt MacDougall
videos.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, my guest is Dr. Matthew MacDougall, a neurosurgeon at Neuralink. We discuss how brain-machine interfaces could help people with paralysis control computers using their intended movements, and how robotic surgery enables the placement of tiny electrodes in the brain. We also explore advances in brain tumor surgery, implant safety, how the brain and software learn to work together, and the role of animal research. Dr. MacDougall shares his vision for future applications, including restoring movement, addressing mental health conditions and expanding human cognition and communication.

Show notes: https://www.hubermanlab.com/episode/essentials-neuralink-and-technologies-to-enhance-human-brains-matthew-macdougall

videos.title: Is Meta’s Muse Wonder model any good?
videos.description:
I put Meta’s new Muse Wonder (and Wonder Full) frontier models through the How I AI bench, which covers nearly 20 tasks across prototyping, agentic workflows, coding, writing, and creative work. I scored everything with an LLM-as-a-judge pass and my own voice notes, then pulled together the first-look results you see here.

*What you’ll learn:*
1. Why Meta’s “personal and professional agent” framing mostly holds up, and where it doesn’t
2. What active focus mode actually does on long-running tasks, and whether it’s real
3. The three agentic tasks where Muse ranked first, and why those categories matter
4. What Muse’s design output actually looks like (it’s not good)
5. How it compares to Sonnet on voice assistant tasks
6. Where Muse lands on SVG and short-form video versus Opus 5.5, Astra, and Fable
7. Whether I’m actually putting Muse into any of my agent workflows

videos.title: Why Failure Hurts More Than It Should
videos.description:
Shopify: The best businesses aren’t built in boardrooms. They’re built by people who just started. Free trial at https://shopify.com/solved
AG1: Visit https://drinkag1.com/solved and get a FREE Immune Support Bundle, including Omega-3 Fish Oil and Vitamin D3+K2, with your first subscription of AG1 Next Gen or AG1 Pro.
One piece of negative feedback from your boss can ruin your whole afternoon. That’s because losing hurts about twice as much as winning feels good, and your brain still treats rejection like a threat to your survival. Drew and I trace this wiring back through history, from monkeys who learned to trade coins for apples and still played it safe, to PGA Tour pros who putt better when they're trying not to lose instead of trying to win.
Get your free episode guide: https://mrk.mn/failureguide.
